title: Johnny Bayersdorffer, the best Dixieland trumpeter
summary: He praises Johnny Bayersdorffer as his idea of a clean Dixieland trumpet, whose OKeh recordings he thinks the best, and says he never got his due.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I guess some of those trumpet players went to Chicago very young or something.

Johnny Baisnautha died lately. Did you know that? Yes. Now there was my idea of a Dixieland trumpet. Yeah. Clean as a pen, every note, and a fine style. And I think of all the recordings that O.K. made here that Johnny Baisnautha made the best. That's my idea.
I like that very much. I like him too. Johnny? Yes.
Very modest man. He worked for the commodity something, I don't know.
Well that record is known the world over whether the people here recognize it or not now.
I like his playing and I like the impression of him. Yeah. We used to get together and chat because we speak the same language.
Well he was a regular guy.
